headline: South Korea beats Czech Republic 2-1 in World Cup opener
summary: The Koreans rallied from a goal down to secure a winning start to their Group A campaign in Guadalajara.
details: South Korea defeated the Czech Republic 2-1 in their World Cup Group A opener on Thursday in Guadalajara, Mexico.
Ladislav Krejci gave the Czechs an early lead in the 59th minute with a header from a long throw, dominating the air throughout the match.
Hwang In-beom equalized eight minutes later after a through ball from Lee Kang-in, curling a right-footed shot into the far corner.
Substitute Oh Hyeon-gyu scored the winning goal, coming on for Son Heung-min, who struggled in front of goal despite having five first-half chances.
The victory puts South Korea on three points, joining Mexico at the top of the pool after Mexico's 2-0 win over South Africa.
The match saw a contrast in styles, with South Korea's technical passing against the Czech Republic's direct, physical approach.
South Korea will next face Mexico on June 18, while the Czech Republic will meet South Africa in Atlanta on the same day.
caption:
A stunning comeback! South Korea rallies from a goal down to beat the Czech Republic 2-1 in their World Cup opener.

South Korea defeated the Czech Republic 2-1 in their World Cup Group A opener on Thursday in Guadalajara, Mexico.

Ladislav Krejci gave the Czechs an early lead in the 59th minute with a header from a long throw, dominating the air throughout the match.

Hwang In-beom equalized eight minutes later after a through ball from Lee Kang-in, curling a right-footed shot into the far corner.

Substitute Oh Hyeon-gyu scored the winning goal, coming on for Son Heung-min, who struggled in front of goal despite having five first-half chances.

The victory puts South Korea on three points, joining Mexico at the top of the pool after Mexico's 2-0 win over South Africa.

The match saw a contrast in styles, with South Korea's technical passing against the Czech Republic's direct, physical approach.

South Korea will next face Mexico on June 18, while the Czech Republic will meet South Africa in Atlanta on the same day.

headline_marked: SpaceX IPO: [[Elon Musk becomes world's first trillionaire]]
headline: SpaceX IPO: Elon Musk becomes world's first trillionaire
summary: Following a record $75 billion SpaceX IPO, Musk's net worth is projected to exceed $1.1 trillion as shares begin trading.
details: Elon Musk has become the world's first trillionaire after SpaceX raised a record $75 billion in its initial public offering (IPO) on Thursday. According to Forbes and Reuters, his net worth is expected to exceed $1.1 trillion when trading begins Friday.

Most of this wealth is tied to SpaceX, where Musk holds a stake worth approximately $866 billion. This follows a previous valuation of $780 billion by Forbes, placing him far ahead of other billionaires like Larry Page and Larry Ellison.

Musk's empire spans multiple industries, including Tesla, the social media platform X (formerly Twitter), and ventures like Neuralink and The Boring Company. His influence is so vast that market observers have termed the network of his businesses the 'Muskonomy'.

Despite his success, Musk faces ongoing criticism regarding his political interventions and governance at his companies. Tesla has also seen weakening sales in some international markets in 2025 due to consumer boycotts.

Investors continue to bet on Musk's vision for space and AI, often referred to as the 'Elon premium'. However, analysts note that SpaceX remains cash-hungry and relies on technologies that may take years to become commercially viable.
caption:
A new era of wealth: Elon Musk has officially become the world's first trillionaire.

Elon Musk has become the world's first trillionaire after SpaceX raised a record $75 billion in its initial public offering (IPO) on Thursday. According to Forbes and Reuters, his net worth is expected to exceed $1.1 trillion when trading begins Friday.

Most of this wealth is tied to SpaceX, where Musk holds a stake worth approximately $866 billion. This follows a previous valuation of $780 billion by Forbes, placing him far ahead of other billionaires like Larry Page and Larry Ellison.

Musk's empire spans multiple industries, including Tesla, the social media platform X (formerly Twitter), and ventures like Neuralink and The Boring Company. His influence is so vast that market observers have termed the network of his businesses the 'Muskonomy'.

Despite his success, Musk faces ongoing criticism regarding his political interventions and governance at his companies. Tesla has also seen weakening sales in some international markets in 2025 due to consumer boycotts.

Investors continue to bet on Musk's vision for space and AI, often referred to as the 'Elon premium'. However, analysts note that SpaceX remains cash-hungry and relies on technologies that may take years to become commercially viable.
